# Notes v1 candidate conformance specimen

This independent private context prepares the saved Foundation consumer-contracts plan's deterministic TRIAL acceptance. It does not edit, build or migrate De Zaaglijst. Publication, public-default promotion and paid coding-agent execution retain their separate gates.

`Notes.Core` owns names, exact owner values, outcomes and semantic capabilities. `Notes` admits commands. `Notes.Api` owns each operation's DTOs and instance endpoint, the public validated identity adaptation and one application problem mapper. `Notes.PostgreSql` owns entities, mappings, native failure classification and atomic head/history/receipt transactions. One bundle selects all three behavior features and the Foundation BFF, JSON, problem and OpenAPI features; the contract-only Core is never activated. The external oracle is not packaged into the application.

Create and rename receipts bind an owner and operation identity to the admitted operation, note ID, expected revision and exact display name. `notes-operation-v1` owns its fixed canonical schema/order. Foundation's bounded incremental writer supplies byte/hash mechanics. Different raw JSON whitespace or GUID spelling is not a different admitted packet; different admitted names or expected revisions are. Replay returns the frozen original acknowledgement even after the current head changes. Changing this identity algorithm requires a separate version. The frozen Workbench canonical/saved fixtures remain unchanged.

Each database operation creates an independent nonpooled context through a tracked shell factory lease. Mutation and fresh receipt reconciliation have separate leases and share the caller-owned outer deadline; retries cannot reset it. Named SQLSTATE/constraint mappings are application policy. Cancellation after commit begins can remain uncertain, and a lost HTTP response never proves rollback. The fixture schema is applied only by the oracle to an explicitly supplied empty disposable database. No initialization service runs during API/metadata composition.

The native schema has a deferred exact head/history foreign key including owner, note ID, revision and name. History and frozen receipts also bind their exact parent/snapshot. EF owns ordinary mappings and write ordering; the deferred head cycle is explicitly SQL-owned. The oracle attempts corrupt head and receipt updates and expects named native constraint failures. A separate coherent but domain-invalid stored name still exercises genuine `ArgumentException` admission and the safe server500 path.

`FixtureAuthenticationAliases` is fixture-only native OIDC claim-action instrumentation. The signed issuer sends untrusted raw aliases distinct from the validated token identity. Those actions must leave Foundation's canonical reserved projection intact; ownership uses only its public reader. This creates a real ownership failure when a compiled seed privately reads raw `iss`/`sub` claims.

List reads apply the authenticated owner on every query, use a UUID keyset cursor and request at most size+1 rows. A cursor grants no ownership. This list shows current note heads; it is not the later immutable evaluation-result delivery protocol. JSON configuration owns request 2MiB, success 1MiB, problem 64KiB, default page100 and maximum requested page500. Names are finite (256 UTF-16 code units); actual worst-case Unicode items and lists qualify the wire budget. Returned page collections own a defensive snapshot. No provider entity or native option enters Core.

Run `python tests/validate_foundation_notes.py --self-test` for source preparation and seeded negatives. These structural checks have deliberately limited claims: compiled graph checks and actual behavior are separate requirements. Seeds contain actual graph/C# violations, not explanatory comments. The new versioned scenario adapter refuses a missing or mismatched Notes oracle and cannot delegate to lending/knowledge oracles.

`--prepare --graph-seed merged-roles|missing-bindings` first compiles the copied specimen, then requires the corresponding evaluated/compiled graph diagnostic. `tests/run_foundation_notes_qualification.py --behavior-seed <name>` restores/builds/packs a separate violating copy, runs the unchanged independent oracle through the real Host/PostgreSQL, and admits only the intended oracle assertion after native process drain and database removal. A compilation or activation failure cannot satisfy behavior rejection. Runtime seeds cover private claim parsing, typed-response provenance bypass, a retained context with actual overlapping `pg_sleep` queries, broad stored-invariant-to400 mapping, and inconsistent conflict envelopes. Positive acceptance remains a separate result. All supplied F6/PK2A/feed/Host arguments are mandatory and exact; no implicit profile is selected.

`--prepare --packages <private-feed> --version <exact-candidate> --dotnet <selected-dotnet> --sdk-working-directory <selected-cwd> --nuget-config <explicit-dependency-sources>` restores, compiles, validates actual assembly boundaries and packs only in a new artifacts directory. Preserve the qualified CShells/Nuplane preview sources through the explicit configuration; the runner adds its private package mapping and isolated cache. All Foundation dependencies are public PackageReferences bound to the selected candidate; no Foundation source projects are referenced. Prepared evidence alone is not TRIAL qualification.

After F6 and PK2A pass, `--qualify` additionally requires `--host <actual-Foundation-Host.dll>`, `--f6-evidence <matching-passed-F6-result.json>`, `--development-profile <prepared-PK2A-directory>` and `--profile-identity <explicit-named-development-profile>`. The accompanying preserved F6 input manifest and PK2A verification must bind exactly the same Host hash and complete candidate feed bytes. Pass the original F6 feed as `--packages`; the runner adds Notes packages only to its own copy. Supply `NOTES_ORACLE_CONNECTION` and `NOTES_ORACLE_DISPOSABLE=true` only for a newly created empty PostgreSQL database. The runner uses the actual Host/Nuplane package feed, native signed RSA OIDC/PKCE/cookie flow, actual HTTP and PostgreSQL. The independent oracle checks owner isolation, every admitted replay packet field, original acknowledgement replay, concurrent expected revisions, transaction rollback after receipt insertion failure, retry after a deliberately lost successful response, bounded pages including a 500-item worst-case Unicode page and uniform safe 400/401/403/404/405/409/413/503/500 envelopes. It writes no paid-worker manifest or release receipt.

Qualification executes a hash-verified Host runtime snapshot in its own retained run directory.
Nuplane state, package installation and active stores also remain there. The complete input feed
retains Host-provided CShells contract archives for restore and proof; runtime package discovery
omits those archives so the native Host provides their shared assembly identity.
Inherited CShells/Foundation/Nuplane configuration environment overrides are removed from owned Host processes before adding the disposable connection. Retained shell and loader settings therefore describe the actual fixture inputs. The wrapper uses the immutable PostgreSQL16 image in an owned container with tmpfs storage and no persistent or host-bound volumes; it records process drain and verified container removal even when acceptance fails.

Remaining acceptance must be recorded honestly: private packaged restore/build, actual Host/PostgreSQL execution, seeded compiled/behavior mutations where useful, F6/PK2A dependency evidence and human responsibility review. No completed qualification is claimed by the scenario's preparation status.
